By Brittany Carter

Topic:Netball

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 6:33pm

Sun 5 Jul 2026 at 9:20am

The Adelaide Thunderbirds celebrate winning a third Super Netball title. (Getty: Daniel Pockett)

A dynasty is well and truly in motion at the Adelaide Thunderbirds.

Defeating the Melbourne Vixens 61- 40 in this year's grand final in front of 10,040 fans at John Cain Arena, the Thunderbirds became the first team to claim three premierships in the Super Netball competition.

The 21-goal margin was also the largest of any decider in this national netball league era.

Ahead of the Super Netball Grand Final, Adelaide Thunderbirds shooter Elmeré van der Berg addresses the misconceptions about her 'resting bitch face' that had people doubting her ability to succeed in the world's best league.

It caps off an extremely dominant year by the minor premiers, who dropped one match all season.

Even the next-best team in the competition couldn't match them for longer than 15 minutes of game time.

It was a tight contest in the opening quarter as the Vixens managed to restrict access to Thunderbirds goal shooter Elmeré van der Berg and take a small lead into the first break, 12-11.

But once Van der Berg corrected her hold it became very difficult to slow down the Thunderbirds in attack.

As the South African import found her rhythm under the post, the game broke apart.

Coach Tania Obst also moved Latanya Wilson from wing defence into goal defence midway through this period.

The work rate lifted and by half-time, a 13-goal turnaround had the Thunderbirds in the hot seat at 32-20.

Adelaide Thunderbirds teammates celebrate victory. (Getty: Daniel Pockett)

Although the Vixens made 26 changes to their team, they could not shift momentum.

Suddenly, the biggest game of the year had gone from being entertainingly close to a one-sided match.

It was a similar pattern to the major semifinal, where the Thunderbirds also beat the Vixens, 58-44.

The losing side lost their way in the second term.

The Vixens could not keep up with the speed of the game, or adapt in real time.

Vixens teammates look dejected after their defeat in the Super Netball grand final. (Getty: Daniel Pockett)

As a result, the timing was off and the Vixens started to rack up a higher penalty count.

Ultimately, they were beaten in every area of the court, dropping their heads and lacking self-belief.

So what is it that makes the Thunderbirds so much better than anyone else?

It helps that they've been able to retain a core group of players that won back-to-back titles in 2023 and 2024.

Last year, they were missing Shamera Sterling-Humphrey for the majority of the season due to pregnancy.

As soon as the Jamaican goal keeper was back in the mix it was clear they would be in with another chance.

In her absence fellow Jamaican Sunshine Girl, Latanya Wilson had to step up as the last line of defence.

Her game grew. Now both of these defenders are equally as strong and compliment each other.

They are light on their feet, play off the body, have incredible closing speed and can out jump tall shooters.

You often hear players speak about the fun environment at Thunderbirds.

It makes a huge difference when you enjoy playing with your mate on court.

The depth of this team goes beyond the bench as well.

Not only do they have players ready to come on at any given moment and inject themselves into the contest.

They are the only team in the competition with a true WD / GD and WA / GA swing.

Wilson and Georgie Horjus are at the peak of their powers across two positions.

Obst has forced them to adapt quickly by shuffling them around on a weekly basis.

Georgie Horjus competes during the Super Netball grand final. (Getty Images: Daniel Pockett)

Already warmed up, with a feel for the game, we tend to see them move from outside to inside the circle in the second-half.

The switch at both ends is seamless and opens up opportunity for fresh legs in the midcourt.

But Horjus and Wilson didn't arrive at the Thunderbirds with this ability. It has been taught within the set-up.

The way the club continues to stretch its players and push them further has made a palpable difference. It's not enough to be great at one position and pretty good at another.

Sensing a need for a defensive change earlier in the finals, Obst pulled the trigger on Wilson a quarter ahead of schedule. On both occasions it paid off.

Wilson ended up crowned as player of the match with seven gains, three intercepts, six deflections, two rebounds and five pick-ups.

Latty Wilson was lethal in defence for the Thunderbirds. (Getty: Daniel Pockett)

Towards the end, coach Obst didn't hesitate to take her big names off and allow the younger ones a run on court.

"The game has really changed from when a seven would start and a seven would finish," Obst said in the post-match press conference referring to the rolling subs now in Super Netball.

"Obviously the two-point [super shot] time has played into that as well, but these athletes train so hard and the depth that we have is so good, so it is about where we can make impact.

"The changes became planned almost, some were about reading the game, some were about getting time into athletes but we know what everyone's strengths are."

The Thunderbirds were up by such a significant margin, they could afford to finish the grand final with Kate Heffernan, Lauren Frew and Elmeré van der Berg on the bench. (Getty: Kelly Defina)

It is also worth noting the Thunderbirds have won three premierships in the past four years with three different goal shooters.

In 2023, England's Eleanor Cardwell joined the club and delivered. In 2024, it was Jamaican Romelda Aiken-George. And now in 2026, South African Van Der Berg has risen to the occasion.

A nod to their spine, defensive structures and the way they work together as a team.

But hopefully next season they won't need to chase after another big recruit. The player signing window is due to open soon and the coach has indicated her desire to keep the team together.

Despite their success on court tonight, Obst revealed it was a difficult lead-up behind the scenes.

Head coach Tania Obst celebrates with Georgie Horjus and Tayla Williams. (Getty: Daniel Pockett)

"I thought we were a bit nervous and clunky in that first quarter and once we ran out some of that, we started to make our adjustments and our second quarter was unbelievable.

"The Vixens were playing a bit differently in defence and so we needed to recognise that and I challenged Elmeré with a couple of things and she did adjust so it was more about seeing and reading the game.

"I didn't really enjoy this week, we had people sick, people roll an ankle, I allowed myself to think about what ifs rather than keeping to the process, but what I do know is this team is sensational.

"Each year, Super Netball is really different ... But I think this team this year, the adaptability, the flexibility, but also the competitive desire individually and collectively is something I don't think I've experienced before."

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 11:07pm

By Brittany Carter

Thank you for tuning into ABC Sport's Super Netball live blog. More game analysis will be added to the top of this article in due course. The season may be done for the year but we will have plenty more netball stories coming your way ahead of the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. The Aussie Diamonds are hoping to try and defend their gold medal at the major tournament. If you missed it, here is the team announcement. We'll catch you then. Congratulations to the Thunderbirds!

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 11:04pm

By Brittany Carter

Congratulations girls. Well done!🥇So, so good! !

- C Slater

The Adelaide Thunderbirds were well and truly the defining team of 2026! No body else could match their dominance and that showed in their winning margins. Throughout the regular season they often got so far out in front that they could rest their big names and offer opportunity to younger players. That bode well for them in the grand final. Imagine getting every single one of their players on court in such a big game. Making everyone feel part of it. They will absolutely celebrate this one hard! And so should all of you Thunderbirds fans!

Key Event

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 9:47pm

By Brittany Carter

It's now confirmed. This 21-goal margin is the largest grand final victory in Super Netball history. It marks the Adelaide Thunderbirds' seventh national league title across all eras.

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 9:44pm

By Brittany Carter

Well that was a bit awkward. The Thunderbirds co-captains were brought up on stage and handed the trophy but nobody let them speak. The canons with pink confetti went off and then someone remembered and handed over the microphone. They deserve a chance as champions to have their say. Even if it has happened in the wrong order.

Sterling-Humphrey thanks the team's fans and sponsors. Horjus thanks the Thunderbirds staff.

"Firstly what a great game of netball we witnessed today ... Thank you to our fans for travelling over, it felt like a home game tonight. We did it!"

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 9:33pm

By Brittany Carter

Kate Moloney congratulates the winning team.

"I just want to start by saying a massive congratulations to [coach] Tania and [co-captains] Shamera and Georgie. You guys have been the team to beat this year, you were far too good for us tonight ... To our fans, this one hurts us. You've helped us reach 10,000 members, something we've never done before. I'm so sorry for the game that we played today. But we'll be back bigger and better next year. I thought the atmosphere tonight was absolutely amazing and what makes our sport so great."

Key Event

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 9:30pm

By Brittany Carter

Defender Latanya Wilson spots herself on the big screen and has the crowd laughing with a cheeky wink. Moments later she is named the Grand Final MVP and dances around with her Jamaican teammate Shamera Sterling-Humphrey. This is why everybody loves this team. They know how to have fun.

Key Event

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 9:24pm

By Brittany Carter

A staggering 19 penalties different in this match. That has gotta hurt. The Vixens did not get their timing right and that was clear with the advanced penalties to Ellis. She had 20 penalties in total. But their captain Moloney (15) and veteran defender Weston (16) also drew too much of the umpire's attention. That gain stat is also crazy. 24 gains to the Thunderbirds. They had three times more than the Vixens. It shows how dominant they were in defence and how clean they were in the contest.

That centre pass to goal stat feels criminal from the Vixens. They are usually so clinical but tonight their attack left a lot to be desired. Only converting 45 per cent. I wouldn't be surprised if the players avoid watching this one back.

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 9:18pm

By Brittany Carter

Fantastic we should be very proud

- Phil

I take it you're a TBirds fan, Phil?

Co-captain Georgie Horjus says it's: "A pinch me moment."

A three-time premiership player inside four seasons. It's very impressive!

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 9:14pm

By Brittany Carter

Well done Thunderbirds watching score from Cambodia such a great result

- sue

Thanks for tuning in from overseas, Sue! What a performance from the minor premiers. They absolutely blew the Vixens out of the water. No competition. They set the benchmark this season and they continue to do that in the decider.

Key Event

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 9:12pm

By Brittany Carter

The dynasty is official!!! Is there a team more dominant than the Thunderbirds in world netball right now?

They have broken history tonight in more ways than one. They now have more Super Netball premierships than anyone else in this modern era. Plus this is thought to be a record margin for a grand final game.

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 9:12pm

By Brittany Carter

With thirty seconds to go, Austin edges the deficit back by two.

SCORE: TBirds lead 61-40

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 9:10pm

By Brittany Carter

With just two and a half minutes left to play, Horjus lines up her team's first super shot of the night. How incredible is this scoreline considering they have not scored a two-point goal until now. Complete dominance.

SCORE: TBirds lead 61-38

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 9:08pm

By Brittany Carter

Kayla Graham enters the court for the first time tonight. She's the only player that hasn't played in every match for the TBirds this season. They've had so much rotation this year but often Graham has been left to ride the bench. Now the margin is out so much though, they can afford to get the 22-year-old South Australian on court. She replaces Van Der Berg at GS. The South African embraces her close friend and New Zealand import Heffernan on the bench. They know they've won this.

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 9:05pm

By Brittany Carter

Ahead of the final super shot period, Honey has said "C'mon, let's go for it." I love her optimism, but surely the Vixens don't have a chance from here? They'll have to absolutely shoot the lights out with the two-point shots. And their accuracy is only sitting at 76 per cent for the game with six and a half minutes to go.

Coming out of the break, the TBirds shift Casey into centre and give Heffernan a rest on the bench.

SCORE: TBirds lead 56-35

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 9:03pm

By Brittany Carter

Midway through the final quarter and the result is clear. The TBirds can soak up this victory now for the final seven minutes. They're out by 20 goals. Just wow.

SCORE: TBirds lead 55-35

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 9:01pm

By Brittany Carter

Ellis is in trouble with the umpires. In quick succession she's taken out another TBirds player with late timing. Flying out of the circle, she wipes out Horjus and the umpire advances the penalty to inside the TBirds' circle. It could have and maybe should have been a two-minute suspension for dangerous play, repeatedly taking out the landing space of the opposition.

The Vixens recognise they need to take Ellis off the court and so Mannix replaces her at GK as we enter the final 10 minutes of the match.

Key Event

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 8:58pm

By Brittany Carter

The official crowd for the 2026 Super Netball Grand Final is 10,040. It's the highest ever netball crowd at John Cain Arena. The first time the sport has cracked 10k here. There was a lot of talk about the Vixens having home crowd advantage in Melbourne, with the venue for this game locked in before the season start as part of Netball Australia's sponsorship with Visit Victoria. But the crowd seems to have plenty of pink! No way to know the actual split, but a heap of Thunderbirds fans must have made the trip interstate to cheer on their team.

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 8:57pm

By Brittany Carter

Ellis was late to a challenge on Heffernan and the umpire has advanced the penalty to inside the circle. Bad timing there led to a collision on the TBirds centre.

SCORE: TBirds lead 47-31

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 8:54pm

By Brittany Carter

Her team may have dropped their heads, they look seriously deflated, but Vixens coach Di Honey still believes her team can win. She's made a host of changes for the final quarter. Austin is on the bench, Graham is at GA. Walters shifts into WD.

"We have absolutely nothing to lose ... You are in this, I know it doesn't feel like it, but let's play this last quarter and win this last quarter like Vixens do."

Key Event

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 8:50pm

By Brittany Carter

Another quarter where the TBirds have had a strangehold on the Vixens and they fail to reach double digits. A 13-9 quarter the way of the team in pink. This match is almost tied up already and we've still got 15 minutes to play. This game has been played at such a high intensity and such a speed that I'll be honest, it's been quite difficult to blog! No other match throughout the 2026 finals series has felt this quick. The TBirds are on another level tonight. Based on this form, I don't think any team would have stood a chance.
